tasks.short: Examine claim forms and records to decide insurance coverage.

steps.what: Open the claim and check submitted documents
Extract policy terms and relevant claim facts

loop.output: coverage fact sheet with quoted source locations
loop.check: claims adjuster compares each extracted fact with the source record
loop.stop: stop on missing pages, conflicting versions, or unclear exclusions; return the case for manual review
loop.why_not_simpler: Policy wording and claim evidence are unstructured and vary by case.

steps.what: Interpret coverage and decide the file position
Record rationale and request missing evidence

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} flow checks that a claim form, policy version, and documents are present in the {OTHER} claim record. A bounded extraction creates a cited coverage fact sheet from {DOCS}; the claims adjuster alone decides coverage and confirms the stored rationale.
tasks.previous_blocker: The evidence and policy wording sit in case-specific documents, so staff must assemble them before applying judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Required-field checks and bounded extraction can prepare the evidence without deciding coverage.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous exclusions, disputed facts, and the accountability for a coverage decision remain with the claims adjuster.
tasks.human_edge: The claims adjuster interprets evidence, policy intent, and the effect of a decision on a claimant.

ambition.what: Review a daily queue of incomplete coverage files before they become delayed claims.

tasks.altitude: The claims adjuster spends less time locating clauses and more time deciding borderline coverage and improving evidence requests.

reach.task: Identify recurring wording or evidence gaps
reach.learn: Read policy versions and classify recurring coverage exceptions.

evidence.claim: Claims software can guide intake and prepare a case record.
A coverage decision still requires human interpretation of evidence and policy wording.
A significant automated coverage decision needs legal review.

assumptions: The workflow begins when a claim form arrives and ends with a versioned coverage rationale in the claim record.
The structured input contract is claim identifier, policy version, loss date, claimant name, document type, document version, and intake status; the claims intake team produces these fields.
Missing fields are entered manually. Scanned documents are extracted only to a fact sheet and move to manual review when a page or policy version is missing.
Native {OTHER} claim-system rules for mandatory fields are tested before custom code.
Two hours per 100 baseline hours are allowed for exception review and maintaining extraction rules.
unknowns: The current claim-system fields and document access rights.
The rate of incomplete claim forms and the cases where legal review is required.
research_questions: Which policy lines have stable clause structures?
How often do adjusters change a prepared coverage fact sheet?

already_counted.description: Review extracted facts and the generated case rationale

incremental.description: Maintain evidence-request rules and review extraction exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes more incomplete documents and policy exceptions; two focal-role upkeep hours per 100 baseline hours are deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyse investigation information and report findings and recommendations.

steps.what: Collect investigator reports, images, and witness records
Reconcile findings against claim facts and policy

loop.input: investigation bundle, policy wording, and claim file
loop.output: finding map showing supported, conflicting, and missing facts
loop.check: claims adjuster checks each finding against the source document
loop.stop: stop when sources conflict or the evidence is incomplete; mark the item for investigation
loop.why_not_simpler: The source material is mixed free text, images, and case-specific evidence.

steps.what: Draft findings and recommendations for the case

loop.input: checked finding map and report template
loop.check: claims adjuster verifies every conclusion, recommendation, and cited fact
loop.stop: stop if a conclusion lacks evidence; retain the template and request more investigation
loop.why_not_simpler: The report needs case-specific narrative from unstructured investigation material.

steps.what: Recommend next action and submit the report

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} flow builds an investigation bundle from the {OTHER} claim file and source documents in {DOCS}. It can reconcile facts and draft a report, but the claims adjuster validates the evidence and submits the recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Investigation material arrives in different formats and the report depends on case-specific judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded reconciliation can make gaps and contradictions visible before the report is written.
tasks.still_hard: A recommendation about liability, fraud, or settlement cannot be inferred safely from an incomplete file.
tasks.human_edge: The claims adjuster assesses credibility, materiality, and the fairness of the recommended next action.

ambition.what: Run a daily evidence-gap review so investigators receive focused follow-up requests.

tasks.altitude: The claims adjuster moves from copying evidence into reports to testing the reasoning and directing further investigation.

reach.learn: Use an evidence map and document preservation rules.

evidence.claim: A bounded document workflow can assemble evidence and draft a report for human validation.

assumptions: The workflow begins with submitted investigation material and ends when a claims manager receives a versioned report.
The structured input contract is claim identifier, source type, source version, investigator, received date, and evidence status; the investigator or claims adjuster supplies these fields.
E-mail attachments and scans are stored as source documents; unreadable or conflicting material is marked for manual review.
Native case-record templates are tested before a custom report builder.
Two hours per 100 baseline hours cover report-template updates and reconciliation exceptions.
unknowns: Which document types can be read from the claim record.
The proportion of reports that require legal or fraud-specialist review.
research_questions: How often does a prepared finding map reveal missing evidence?
Which report sections have an approved template?

already_counted.description: Check the reconciled finding map and report draft

incremental.description: Review recurring reconciliation errors and update report templates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes mixed evidence and more report corrections; two focal-role upkeep hours per 100 baseline hours are deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pay and process claims within the designated authority level.

steps.what: Check settlement, payee, and authority limit
Create the payment instruction in the claim record
Handle rejected payments and update the file

tasks.design: A configured {OTHER} claim record checks payment amount and authority before creating an internal payment instruction for the {BANK} process. The claims adjuster approves the exact payment-instruction version; rejected payments return as a tracked exception.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payment checks, authority limits, and finance handoff are often checked across separate records.
tasks.enabler_now: Required fields, authority tables, and an internal payment interface can remove re-keying without removing approval.
tasks.still_hard: Payee changes, settlements outside authority, and payment exceptions need an accountable claims adjuster.
tasks.human_edge: The claims adjuster checks whether the settlement, payee, and authority are appropriate before money moves.

ambition.what: Review the daily rejected-payment queue before a claimant experiences a further delay.

tasks.altitude: The claims adjuster stops re-keying routine payments and focuses on authority exceptions and failed-payment causes.

reach.learn: Read payment status codes and match them to the approved instruction.

evidence.claim: A claims record can guide intake and case processing.
A payment instruction can be checked against configured authority limits before human approval.

assumptions: The workflow begins with an approved settlement and ends when the payment status returns to the claim record.

The structured input contract is claim identifier, settlement version, approved amount, payee identifier, currency, authority limit, and payment status; the claims adjuster and finance team produce these fields.
The payment interface only writes an internal instruction. Any changed amount, payee, or settlement version voids the approval and requires a new check.
Native authority controls and payment export configuration are tested before custom integration.
Three hours per 100 baseline hours cover authority-table maintenance and payment-exception review.
unknowns: Whether the claim record exposes authority limits and payment statuses.
Which payment changes require a second approver under the insurer's policy.
research_questions: What proportion of payment instructions fail validation?
Can finance return a reason code for every rejected payment?

already_counted.description: Approve the versioned payment instruction and review payment exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain authority limits and review recurring payment failures

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes a material share of payments fail checks and need correction; three focal-role upkeep hours per 100 baseline hours are deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Investigate, evaluate, and settle claims fairly and promptly.

steps.what: Plan the investigation from the claim file

loop.input: claim facts, policy wording, and prior correspondence
loop.check: claims adjuster checks the checklist before asking any party for information
loop.stop: stop for suspected fraud, serious injury, or contradictory facts; route for specialist handling
loop.why_not_simpler: The needed evidence depends on the facts and policy terms of each claim.

steps.what: Speak with the claimant and relevant parties
Evaluate liability and negotiate a fair settlement
Draft the settlement record and follow-up

loop.input: settlement position, checked notes, and approved template
loop.check: claims adjuster checks amounts, promises, and factual statements before saving
loop.stop: stop when terms are disputed or the template does not cover the case; write the record manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Settlement records need a case-specific account of a human conversation and agreement.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} flow prepares an investigation checklist from the {OTHER} claim record and stores checked contact notes. It leaves claimant conversations, liability evaluation, and settlement negotiation with the claims adjuster, while drafting the settlement record in {DOCS} for review.
tasks.previous_blocker: The most valuable work is a case-specific investigation and difficult human conversation, not a repeatable form.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded checklist and draft record can reduce preparation and post-call administration.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, negotiation, disputed facts, and fair settlement decisions remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: The claims adjuster builds trust, tests credibility, and negotiates an outcome that a claimant can understand.

ambition.what: Give claimants with complex cases a clearer evidence checklist before their first detailed conversation.

tasks.altitude: The claims adjuster spends more of the week on complex conversations and settlement quality rather than gathering files and writing notes.

reach.task: Identify recurrent loss patterns from settled claims
reach.learn: Interpret claim evidence and settlement reasons without exposing personal details.

evidence.claim: Claims tools can support guided intake and prepare evidence for review, but settlement conversations require human judgement.
A checklist and record draft can prepare rather than replace a claims conversation.

assumptions: The workflow begins when a complex claim is assigned and ends when the checked settlement record is stored.

The structured input contract is claim identifier, policy version, loss type, claimant contact preference, investigation status, and settlement status; the claims intake team and claims adjuster produce these fields.
Conversation recordings or notes are not sent to a model by default. A role holder selects only the necessary checked notes for a draft.
Existing case checklists and templates are configured before custom drafting support.
One hour per 100 baseline hours covers checklist and template maintenance.
unknowns: Which claim types require legal, medical, or fraud-specialist participation.
Whether callers consent to recording and how contact notes are retained.
research_questions: Which evidence requests recur most often in complex claims?
How much time is spent writing post-call settlement records?

already_counted.description: Review the prepared investigation checklist and settlement-record draft

incremental.description: Maintain evidence checklists and settlement-record templates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most time remains in investigation, conversation, and negotiation; one focal-role upkeep hour per 100 baseline hours is deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Lead evidence quality, difficult conversations, and settlement consistency rather than copying documents between claim records.
reach: Support insurance underwriters with recurring coverage and loss-pattern evidence.
Work with finance on payment-exception causes.
role.ambitious_version: A claims service that resolves complete, straightforward files faster while giving complex claimants better evidence requests and more time with an accountable adjuster.
